name: What is the difference between standard drywall finishing and a Level 5 finish?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between standard drywall finishing and a Level 5 finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard finish features joint compound feathered over seams and fasteners, usually topped with an orange peel or knockdown texture to mask subtle surface variations. A Level 5 drywall finish includes an entire skim coat of joint compound applied across every square inch of the drywall surface, followed by fine sanding. Homeowners choose Level 5 when installing high-gloss paint, non-textured modern walls, or rooms with harsh directional natural light. Level 5 requires significantly more labor and time, while textured drywall is faster and more forgiving.
acceptedAnswer.description: A standard finish covers seams and fasteners under texture, while a Level 5 finish covers the entire wall in a skim coat of mud for a completely flat, non-textured surface.
